meta.title: Why Roman Buildings Stand for 2,000 Years But Ours Crumble #shorts
meta.description:
Have you ever wondered why modern concrete bridges crumble after just a few decades, while ancient Roman structures are still standing strong after two thousand years? For centuries, scientists were completely baffled by this mystery. But they recently discovered a hidden ingredient that changes everything. See those tiny white chunks inside ancient Roman concrete? Researchers used to think they were just a sign of poor mixing. It turns out, they are "lime clasts." When a crack forms and rainwater seeps in, it dissolves these lime chunks, recrystallizing them to literally glue the crack back shut. Yes, Roman concrete actually heals itself. Modern engineering is only now trying to copy this ancient recipe to build cities that last forever. Would you live in a self-healing concrete house?
